# hookdoctor

hookdoctor diagnoses why a Claude Code hook did not fire. It loads hooks from
the user, project and local settings layers and validates them statically:
settings JSON, event names, matcher regexes, command resolution, executable
bits. With the opt-in -exec flag it also dry-runs each hook with a synthetic
payload matching the documented event schema and validates the output
contract. It reports a named cause and fix for the failure modes it covers.

- Causes detected: invalid-json, unknown-event, bad-matcher, bad-type,
  empty-command, command-not-found, command-is-dir, not-executable, timeout,
  invalid-json-output, crash, blocking-exit.
- It never modifies settings or hooks. execution is opt-in via -exec; nothing runs without it. -exec runs the hook commands, which are arbitrary code (including any network calls they make); it is not a sandbox.
- Output: text or JSON. Exit 1 on any error-level finding.

## Usage

- `go install github.com/ofershap/hookdoctor@v0.1.0 && hookdoctor check`
- Flags: -root, -event, -no-exec, -settings, -format (text|json), -max-timeout
